backgrounds: Single set for the entire episode: a cozy living room where a stop-motion couple sits side by side on a gray upholstered couch. The room reads as a modest, lived-in home interior with a beige/taupe wall, a white paneled door/closet on the left, a wainscoted wall section and a small floating wood shelf with a potted plant on the right, and a curtained window (sheer cream curtains) visible in some wider/side angles. A framed black-and-white picture hangs on the back wall, and a small side table with a framed family photo sits at the edge of frame near the couch. The video opens and closes on plain black title cards (text-only, no set) for the show/episode branding, but the story content itself never leaves this one living-room location, only shifting between wide two-shot and tighter single-character coverage of the same space.
props: Two smartphones (one lighter/silver held by the woman, one black held by the man) that both characters are glued to
Wooden coffee table in front of the couch
TV remote control with multicolored buttons on the coffee table
Folded newspaper/magazine on the coffee table
Small white plastic object (possibly a phone charger/pill case) and a couple of yellow/red small objects on the coffee table
Tall tripod floor lamp with fabric drum shade, lit, on the right side of the couch
Framed family photograph on a small side table next to the couch
Framed black-and-white artwork/photo on the back wall
Small potted plant on a floating shelf
Gray fabric couch with visible tufted/stitched cushions
lighting_notes: Warm, soft interior lighting dominated by the practical floor lamp glowing on camera right, creating a cozy amber pool of light against cooler gray-beige walls. Overall exposure is fairly dim/moody (evening indoor feel) with soft falloff and shallow depth of field that blurs the background, keeping focus on the characters' faces. The phone screens add a small cool blue glow reflected on the characters' hands/faces, contrasting with the warm lamp light -- a deliberate warm/cool contrast that visually reinforces the phones-versus-real-life theme.
color_palette: muted gray (couch, walls, felted character skin tones by contrast)
small cool blue accent (phone screen glow)
visual_complexity_notes: The set is minimal and tightly controlled: one room, one couch, one coffee table, a handful of clearly chosen props (phone, remote, newspaper, lamp, family photo). Background elements are soft-focus and understated rather than cluttered, which keeps all visual attention on the two felt-textured stop-motion character faces and their phones. This restraint looks deliberate -- it supports a simple, single-joke premise (people ignoring each other for their phones) without needing scene changes, and the shallow-focus, warm-lamp lighting further isolates the characters from an otherwise plain, low-detail backdrop.
